frames.narration: Transfer 100 from Bank A to Bank B. The coordinator starts a transaction involving both databases.
Phase 1, prepare. The coordinator asks both participants whether they can commit.
Each participant does the work, writes it to its durable log, locks the account, and votes yes. That vote is a promise it can keep even after a crash.
Everyone voted yes. The coordinator writes 'commit' to its own durable log. From this moment the transaction is decided.
Phase 2, commit. The coordinator tells both participants to commit. They apply the change, release the locks and acknowledge.
Now the failure case: suppose Bank B had voted NO (not enough room, an error). The coordinator would send abort to both, and Bank A would roll back its debit. Neither change happens.

The dangerous failure: the coordinator crashes after the votes but before announcing the decision. Both participants voted yes, so they cannot commit or abort on their own, and they keep their locks until the coordinator is back. This is the blocking problem.
